quandoUsar: Show live what an agent is doing on a long task: each step has a type (`search`, `read`, `write`, `think`, `run`) that picks the icon.
Steps that collect short findings, such as files, sites or results: they appear as chips, one by one, as the `items` list grows.
Runs with many steps, where finished steps should fold into a single line with a count and total time, and reopen on demand.
quandoEvitar: Use `todo-list` when the whole plan is known from the start and you only need to mark each step as pending, in progress or done.
Use `tool-result` when you need to show the full input and output of each tool call.
Use `loading-states` for a short wait, with no steps to list.

teclado.acao: With focus on the summary line, opens or closes the list of finished steps.
Moves focus to the summary line, the component's only control; it exists only after the first step finishes.

acessibilidade: The root is a `<section>` with `aria-label` equal to `title`; the summary is a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, and the collapsed list is `inert`.
An invisible `role="status"` region announces the title of the running step and, at the end, how many steps finished; pending and failed steps get a screen-reader-only suffix.
The fixed texts (“steps finished”, “Done”, “(waiting)”, “(failed)”) are in English in the code and have no translation prop.
movimento: On the running step, a ring pulses around the icon and a shimmer runs across the title; chips enter one by one with a short spring, without overshoot.
When a step finishes, it leaves the live list and folds into the summary line with a height spring, while the finished count rolls to the new value.
With “reduce motion” on, the pulse, shimmer and spin stop, heights change instantly and chips appear without animation.
responsivo: Fills 100% of the parent's width: the header and each step's `detail` truncate with an ellipsis on one line, while the step title and chips wrap.
notasIA: It is data-driven: pass `steps` with a stable `id` and update `status` (`pending`, `running`, `done`, `error`), `items` and `duration` while the agent works; the component does not measure time itself.
Each text in `items` is used as the chip's `key`: do not repeat the same text within a step.
Finished steps start collapsed; use `defaultExpanded` or the `expanded` and `onExpandedChange` pair to open them, for example when a step ends with `error`.

quandoUsar: An assistant that sits beside the content it comments on (document, dashboard, editor) and pushes the page instead of covering it.
Short, contextual conversations about the current screen, with ready-made suggestions that send the prompt in one tap.
Split layouts: the panel chooses between docking and overlaying based on the width of its own container, not the window.
quandoEvitar: Use `chat-app` when the conversation is the whole screen, with a conversation list and replies that can be stopped or redone.
Use `drawer` for a temporary side panel that is not a conversation.
Use `prompt-input` with `message-scroller` when you need attachments, a model menu or a stop button: the prompt box built in here only sends text.

teclado.acao: In the prompt box, sends the text; during IME composition it does not send.
Inserts a line break without sending.
With focus inside the panel, closes the panel.
On a suggestion, sends its text as the prompt.
Moves through close, suggestions, prompt box and send; with the panel closed, nothing inside it receives focus.

acessibilidade: The panel is an `<aside>` labeled by the title; on open, focus goes to the prompt box and, on close, returns to the element that had it before, if it still exists (the built-in `launcher` leaves the DOM when the panel opens, so it does not get focus back).
The message list is `aria-live="polite"` and each message carries a screen-reader-only prefix; when closed, the panel is `inert`, and when open in overlay mode, the page behind it is `inert`.
Labels such as “Close”, “Send message”, “Conversation” and “Suggestions” are fixed in English; `title`, `subtitle`, `placeholder` and `emptyText` are yours.
movimento: When docked, the panel opens with a width spring and pushes the page; when overlaid, it slides over the page with a fading scrim.
New messages rise with a slight scale-up, suggestions enter in sequence when the panel opens, and the list scrolls smoothly to the end on each message.
With “reduce motion” on, the panel, messages and suggestions change state instantly and scrolling to the end is no longer smooth.
responsivo: A `ResizeObserver` measures the container: below `overlayBelow` (640 px by default) the panel slides over the page, with width `min(100%, max(width, 320px))`.
The prompt box grows with the text up to 132 px and then scrolls internally; suggestions stay on a single line, with horizontal scrolling.
desempenho: There are two `ResizeObserver`s per instance (container and list) and the list is not virtualized: very long conversations weigh on the DOM.
notasIA: Wrap the page: `children` is the content beside the panel, and the root uses `height: 100%`, so the parent needs a defined height.

The conversation is yours: pass `messages` (`id`, `role`, `content`), append the message in `onSend` and turn on `pending` until the reply arrives; `content` accepts nodes, such as a `StreamingResponse`.
Use `open` with `onOpenChange` and `launcher={false}` when the page already has its own button; this item depends on `loading-states` for the `pending` indicator.

quandoUsar: An agent proposes an action with a real effect (refund, send, delete) and a person must approve or reject it before it happens.
Requests that need context: a summary, facts as label and value pairs and, optionally, a preview of the change behind the details button.
Review queues where the card stays on screen after the decision, showing what was decided and an “Undo”.
quandoEvitar: Use `tool-approval` for a compact request inside the conversation, with allow once, allow always or deny.
Use `confirm-morph` or `hold-to-confirm` when the person themselves triggers a destructive action and only needs to confirm it.
Use `dialog` when the decision must block the rest of the screen until it is made.

teclado.acao: Activates the focused button: details, reject, approve or undo.
Moves through the controls in DOM order: details button, reject and approve.

acessibilidade: The root is a `<section>` labeled by `title`; the details button exposes `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, and the result appears in a `role="status"` region.
On decision, the pressed button leaves the DOM and the code does not move focus, which lands on `body`; if the queue is used by keyboard, move focus yourself in `onStatusChange`.
“Show details”, “Hide details”, “Undo” and “needs your approval” are fixed in English; only `approveLabel`, `rejectLabel` and `resolvedLabels` can be translated.
movimento: On decision, the icon becomes a check mark or an X that draws itself, a ripple leaves the badge and the buttons give way to the result with a short fade.
The details open with a height spring and the fact rows enter in sequence.
With “reduce motion” on, only opacity changes remain: no ripple, no stroke drawing and no color or scale transitions.
responsivo: When the window is up to 26rem wide (media query, not container), the two buttons split the full row; the card always fills 100% of the parent.
notasIA: The card only records the decision: run the action in `onStatusChange` and, to reflect what the server replied, control `status` (`pending`, `approved`, `rejected`).
“Undo” returns the card to `pending` and calls `onStatusChange("pending")`; if the action cannot be undone once executed, pass `allowUndo={false}`.
The details button only appears when there are `details` or `children`; each `label` in `details` is used as the `key`, so do not repeat labels.

quandoUsar: AI answers or research texts where each claim points to a numbered source.
When the reader should check the source's title, site and excerpt without leaving the paragraph, and open the original only if they want to.
When there is a list of sources at the end and it should highlight the source of the chip pointed at in the text, and the chip when a row is pointed at.
quandoEvitar: Use `hover-card` for a preview of a person or a standalone link, with no numbering or source list.
Use `tooltip` when the note is just short text, with no link or interactive content.
Sources without an address do not fit here: the address is required, and both the card title and the list row are links to it.

teclado.acao: Moves through the chips in the text and the list rows; focus on a row lights up the chips of the same source.
On a chip, opens the source card and moves focus to it.
On the card title or a list row, opens the source in a new tab.
Closes the card and returns focus to the chip.

acessibilidade: Each chip is a `<button>` with `aria-label` “Source N: title”; the card is a Radix popover (`role="dialog"`) that only receives focus when opened by click or keyboard, never by hover.
The list is a `<section>` labeled by its own title, with an `<ol>` of links that open in a new tab with `rel="noreferrer noopener"`.
The “Source N” labels are fixed in English; the list title comes from the `title` prop of `CitationSources` (default “Sources”).
movimento: The card grows from the chip, with scale and fade, and its rows enter in sequence; the active chip grows slightly.
A single highlight slides between the list rows with a spring, following the pointer, focus or active chip; rows enter staggered on mount.
With “reduce motion” on, the card and rows appear without animation and the highlight switches rows instantly.
responsivo: The card is at most 20rem wide and shrinks with the window; it opens above the chip and Radix repositions it to fit, with 12 px of clearance.
The chip never separates from the preceding word at a line break; in the list, the title truncates at two lines, and in the card the excerpt truncates at four.
notasIA: There are three parts in the same file: `Citations` receives `sources` and wraps the text, `Citation source="id"` goes inside the sentence and `CitationSources` lists everything; the last two throw an error outside `Citations`.
The number comes from the position in `sources` (index + 1), not from the order in which the chip appears in the text; a `source` that does not exist in `sources` renders nothing.
Put `<Citation>` right after the word and before the punctuation; `site` is optional and, without it, the host of `url` is shown.

quandoUsar: Show the change an agent made or proposes to a file, from the before and after text.
Reviews where it matters to see the exact span that changed within the line and how many lines were added and removed.
New, deleted or renamed files: the header gets the “New file”, “Deleted” or “Renamed” label and, in the last case, the previous path.
quandoEvitar: Use `code-block` to show code without a comparison, with a copy button.
Use `image-compare` when the difference is visual, between two images.
For side-by-side diffs, with syntax colors or for huge files, look for another solution: here the diff is unified, without syntax highlighting and computed in the browser.

teclado.acao: Moves through the header buttons, the diff area (which is focusable) and the folded ranges.
Activates the focused button: collapse the file, show or fold all unchanged lines, or open a folded range.
With focus on the diff area, scroll the content; this is the native scrolling of a region with `tabIndex={0}`.

acessibilidade: The diff area is a focusable `role="group"`, labeled with the file name and the counts; numbers and signs are `aria-hidden`, and each changed line starts with “Added:” or “Removed:” for screen readers only.
The header buttons have `aria-label`, `aria-expanded` or `aria-pressed`; when a folded range is opened, focus moves to the revealed lines, because the button stops existing.
With the file collapsed, the body is `inert`; all labels are fixed in English.
movimento: Lines enter in sequence, with a short delay between them (the same from the 25th on), and the five header blocks appear one after another.
The body opens and closes with a height spring; a folded range grows from the 32 px of its own row, without a jump.
With “reduce motion” on, the lines appear all at once and heights change instantly.
responsivo: Long lines do not wrap: the body scrolls horizontally with the number column pinned to the left, and `maxHeight` limits the height and turns on vertical scrolling.
Below 26rem of the component's own width (container query), the five blocks disappear; in the path, the directory truncates with an ellipsis before the file name.
desempenho: The diff is computed in the browser by LCS: after trimming the equal start and end, the table has the size of (middle lines before) × (middle lines after); the result is memoized by `before` and `after`.
There is no virtualization: each visible line is a DOM node; folded unchanged ranges are not rendered, so keep `context` low on large files.
notasIA: Pass `filename`, `before` and `after` with the full text: an empty `before` indicates a new file and an empty `after`, a deleted file; the component does not read a ready-made patch.
`context` (default 3) defines how many equal lines stay around each change; larger spans fold into a clickable line, and a new diff starts folded again.
For several files, render one `FileDiff` per file and use `defaultOpen={false}` or the `open` and `onOpenChange` pair to leave only some open.

quandoUsar: An image request in a conversation or editor, with prompt, progress and result in the same card.
Generations that take a few seconds and have known progress: the card shows the phase and percentage instead of a spinner.
When the result calls for immediate actions: generate again, download the image and copy the prompt.
quandoEvitar: Use `skeleton` to reserve the place of an ordinary image that is just loading.
Use `image-viewer` for a gallery of finished images, with zoom and navigation.
Use `progress` or `toast-progress` for long tasks that do not end in an image.

teclado.acao: Activates the focused button: “Regenerate”, “Copy prompt”, “Generate” or “Try again”.
Activates the “Download” link, which points to `src` with the `download` attribute.

acessibilidade: While generating, the frame is a `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow` and `aria-valuetext` (phase and percentage); at the end, a `role="status"` region announces “Image ready”.
The error appears in a `role="alert"`; the image uses `alt`, which by default repeats the `prompt`, so pass an `alt` that describes the result.
Phases, buttons and announcements are fixed in English; only `prompt`, `model`, `alt` and `error` are yours.
movimento: During generation, a diagonal opacity wave sweeps a grid of 8 × 6 cells, the progress line fills and the phase label swaps, leaving through a blur.
When the image finishes loading, it goes from blurred and slightly enlarged to sharp in under a second, and the actions enter in sequence in the footer.
With “reduce motion” on, the wave stops and the cells stay fixed, the image appears without blur or zoom and swaps are immediate.
responsivo: Fills 100% of the parent and the frame keeps `aspectRatio` (default `4 / 3`); the prompt truncates at two lines and the actions wrap to the line below.
desempenho: Without `status`, a 70 ms `setInterval` moves the progress; each generating card animates 48 cells, and the 28 px blur in the reveal is expensive: avoid several generating at the same time.
notasIA: Without `status`, the card generates nothing: it runs a timed preview of `duration` ms on mount and on each “Regenerate”; in real use, control `status` (`idle`, `generating`, `done`, `error`) and `progress` from 0 to 1.
`onRegenerate` is called by “Generate”, “Regenerate” and “Try again”: trigger the new generation there and swap `src` when it finishes.
The image only appears with `status` at `done` and `src` loaded; “Download” is a link with `download` to the same `src`.

quandoUsar: The interval in which the AI has already received the request and has nothing to show yet.
`ThinkingDots` inside a chat bubble and `ThinkingShimmer` inline, at the point where the reply will start.
Longer waits: `ThinkingPhrases` alternates status phrases and `ThinkingSteps` shows “Step 2 of 5” when the number of steps is known.
quandoEvitar: Use `loader` for generic loading outside AI conversations: spinner, dots, bars, ring and orbit in three sizes.
Use `skeleton` when you can reserve the shape of the content that will arrive.
Use `todo-list` or `agent-activity` when each agent step needs to appear with a name and state.
acessibilidade: Each indicator is a `role="status"`; in the dots and steps the drawing is `aria-hidden`, and the accessible name is the `label` or “Step N of M” followed by the `label`.
In `ThinkingPhrases` the phrase sits inside the `role="status"`, so each change is a live region update: prefer short phrases and a generous `interval`.
The default texts (“Thinking…”, the four phrases, “Step … of …”) are in English: `label` and `phrases` are translatable, the “Step N of M” is not.
movimento: A shimmer sweeps across the letters (`ThinkingShimmer`), three dots rise in a wave (`ThinkingDots`), a dot orbits a ring beside the phrase (`ThinkingPhrases`) and the current step's pip pulses (`ThinkingSteps`).
Phrases, step number and label swap by rising from a light blur and leaving upward; the pips fill with a spring without overshoot.
With “reduce motion” on, each indicator becomes a still, readable state: text without shimmer, still dots and orbit, and immediate text swaps.
responsivo: Phrases and the step label stay on one line and truncate with an ellipsis; `ThinkingSteps` shows one pip per step up to 8 steps and, above that, a single bar.
desempenho: Only `ThinkingPhrases` uses a timer (one `setInterval`, with a minimum of 600 ms); the other indicators are CSS animations.
notasIA: Import the variant directly (`ThinkingShimmer`, `ThinkingDots`, `ThinkingPhrases`, `ThinkingSteps`) or use `LoadingStates` with `variant`; `showLabel` and `duration` exist only on the individual components.
`ThinkingSteps` is controlled: pass `current` (starting at 1) and `total`, and change `label` on each step; out-of-range values are clamped to the valid range.
Mount the indicator only while waiting and swap it for the content when the reply starts; `ai-sidebar` and `chat-app` already depend on this item.

quandoUsar: The assistant's reply in a conversation where it does not use a bubble: avatar, name, formatted text and actions below.
Replies with lists, headings, code, bold and links: `content` accepts a small subset of Markdown.
When each reply needs copy, retry and rating with thumbs up or down.
quandoEvitar: Use `message-bubble` for the person's messages and for bubble-style conversations.
Use `streaming-response` while the text is still arriving word by word.
Use `chat-thread` or `comment-thread` for conversations between people, with reactions, replies and read receipts.

teclado.acao: Moves through the links, the code blocks (focusable for scrolling) and each action button; focus inside the row makes the toolbar appear.
Activates the focused action: copy, retry or rate; repeating the same rating clears it.
With focus on a wide code block, scroll the code horizontally (native scrolling).

acessibilidade: The root is an `<article>` with `aria-label` “Message from” plus the `name`; the avatar is `aria-hidden`.
The toolbar is a `role="toolbar"` in which each button has an `aria-label`; the rating buttons use `aria-pressed`, and a `role="status"` region announces “Message copied”.
On touch screens the toolbar is always visible; with a mouse it appears on hover or when focus enters the row, and a rating already given stays visible.
movimento: On mount, the content blocks enter in sequence, rising from a light blur; `animateIn={false}` turns this off.
The toolbar buttons enter one after another, the copy icon turns into a check mark, the retry icon makes a turn with a spring and the chosen thumb makes a small hop.
With “reduce motion” on, the blocks only fade, with no delay between them, the icons swap with a fade and there is no turn or hop.
responsivo: The grid has the avatar column and a flexible column; long text wraps at any point and the code blocks scroll horizontally instead of widening the page.
notasIA: Pass the text in `content` (paragraphs, lists, headings with `#`, blocks between triple backticks, inline code, `**negrito**` and links `http`, `https`, `mailto`, `/` or `#`); tables and italics come out as plain text.

The retry button only exists with `onRetry`, and the rating ones only with `onRatingChange`, `defaultRating` or `rating={…}` (`rating={null}` counts); `actions="always"` or `"none"` pins or hides the toolbar.
With `children`, you render the content and `content` becomes just the text to copy; in long histories, pass `animateIn={false}`.

quandoUsar: Messenger-style conversations: the person's bubbles sit on the right in the accent color and the assistant's on the left on a neutral surface.
Sequences of messages from the same sender: `MessageBubbleGroup` tightens the inner corners and leaves the tail only on the last bubble.
When the sent message should show time and delivery state (`sending`, `sent`, `delivered`, `read`, `failed`) or the other party is typing (`typing`).
quandoEvitar: Use `message` for long assistant replies, with Markdown and a toolbar for copy, retry and rating.
Use `chat-thread` when you need the ready-made conversation, with reactions, read receipts, typing indicator and input field.
Use `chat-app` when you want the whole chat screen, with conversation list and prompt box.
acessibilidade: Each bubble starts with the author for screen readers only (“You”, “Assistant” or the `author` you pass), and the delivery state has a hidden text equivalent to the ticks.
The typing dots are a `role="status"` with `aria-label` “Typing”; `MessageBubbleGroup` is a `role="group"` that gets its name from `label`.
The bubble does not create a live region for new messages: put the list in a container with that role, such as `message-scroller`, which uses `role="log"`.
movimento: The bubble emerges from the tail corner, growing and rising with a spring with a slight bounce; `animateIn={false}` turns this off for history.
Each new tick draws itself when `status` changes (those already there on mount do not repeat); `sending` shows a small spin and `typing`, three dots in a wave.
With “reduce motion” on, the bubble and ticks only fade, and the spin and dots stay still.
responsivo: The bubble takes at most 82% of the container width, up to 34rem; the text preserves line breaks and breaks long words.
notasIA: Group consecutive messages from the same sender in a `MessageBubbleGroup from="user"`: it sets `from` and `position` on each child, which must be direct `MessageBubble`s (a wrapper in between breaks this).
`timestamp` arrives already formatted (for example “9:41”) and `status` draws the ticks; in a group, pass both only on the last bubble, as the demo does.
For the typing indicator, render a bubble with `typing` and swap it for the message when the text arrives; outside groups, `position` and `tail` control corners and tail.

quandoUsar: The scroll area of a conversation that receives new messages or streaming text and should follow the end while the reader is there.
When scrolling up should release the follow behavior, without pulling the reader back, and offer a shortcut to the latest message.
Live logs in general (run logs, event feeds) where new content enters from the bottom.
quandoEvitar: Use `scroll-area` for static content that only needs thin scrollbars and edge fades.
Use `chat-thread` or `chat-app` when you want the ready-made conversation, with messages and input field, and not just the container.
Use `infinite-masonry` for feeds that load more items on reaching the end, instead of following what arrives.

teclado.acao: With focus on the area, scroll the conversation (native scrolling) and immediately interrupt the automatic slide to the end.
Moves focus to the scroll area, which is focusable, then to whatever is interactive in the messages and to the jump button.
On the “Jump to latest” button, returns to the end; focus moves to the scroll area, because the button disappears.

acessibilidade: The visible area is a focusable `role="region"` named by `label`; the content is a `role="log"` with `aria-live="polite"`, so new messages are announced.
The jump button shows the text of `jumpLabel`, and the counter has an `aria-label` with the number of new messages (in English, with no translation prop).
When the button is activated by keyboard, focus goes to the scroll area instead of being lost when the button leaves.
movimento: New messages rise with a spring and a slight scale-up; those already present on the first render do not animate.
The return to the end is a spring slide in the scroll position; the jump button emerges from below and the unread number rolls to each new total.
With “reduce motion” on, scrolling goes straight to the end, and messages and button only fade.
responsivo: The height comes from `--message-scroller-height` (default 22rem) or from `className` and `style`; scrolling is internal, and the top and bottom edges fade when there is more content in that direction.
desempenho: Two `ResizeObserver`s track the content and the frame; there is no virtualization and each child gets an animated wrapper, so limit the history in very long conversations.
notasIA: Each direct child counts as one message: give each a stable `key`; the unread counter compares the number of children, so trimming old messages while new ones arrive makes it stop going up.

Set the height (variable `--message-scroller-height`, `className` or `style`); `onAtBottomChange` signals when the reader leaves the end or returns, and `threshold` (32 px) says what still counts as the end.
It pairs with `message-bubble` or `message` as children; pass `animateIn={false}` to them, because the animated entrance is already handled here (`animateItems`).

quandoUsar: An assistant's prompt box: grows with the text, sends with Enter and inserts a line break with Shift + Enter.
Replies that can be interrupted: with `running`, the send button becomes a stop button in the same place.
Requests with attachments as chips and a menu to choose the model, all inside the same box.
quandoEvitar: Use `textarea` for a multi-line field in a form, with no send on Enter or stop button.
Use `mention-input` when the text needs mentions of people with @ or channels with #.
Use `chat-app` when you want the whole chat screen, with conversation, streaming replies and prompt box already wired up.

teclado.acao: In the text box, sends when there is text or an attachment; during IME composition it does not send.
Inserts a line break without sending; the box grows up to `maxRows` rows and then scrolls internally.
On the model selector, opens the menu with focus on the first model.
In the menu, moves between models; the arrows wrap from the last to the first.
In the menu, chooses the focused model, closes the menu and returns focus to the selector.
Closes the menu without changing the model and returns focus to the selector.

acessibilidade: The text box is named by `label` (default “Prompt”) and has the hidden description “Press Enter to send, Shift and Enter for a new line.” via `aria-describedby`; the visible hint is `aria-hidden`.
The icon-only buttons have a fixed English `aria-label` (“Attach files”, “Remove …”, “Send prompt”, “Stop response”), the selector announces itself as “Model: …” and the menu is a Radix radio group.
After sending, focus returns to the text box; send and stop are the same `<button>`, which only changes its `aria-label`, and stop is disabled without `onStop`.
movimento: The box follows the text height with a short spring; the attachment tray opens to its own height, each chip enters growing and the others slide when one leaves.
When `running` becomes `true`, the arrow leaves upward, a stop square grows in its place and an arc spins around the button; the model name swaps by sliding vertically.
With “reduce motion” on, the height changes instantly, chips and icons only fade, the arc stops and the menu appears with a quick fade.
responsivo: It is a width container: below 22rem the “Enter to send” hint disappears; the model name truncates with an ellipsis, and so does each attachment name, from 11rem.
The model menu opens above the selector, at least 15rem wide, and Radix repositions it to fit on screen, with 12 px of clearance.
notasIA: Wire up `onSubmit`, which receives the already-trimmed `value`, `attachments` and `model`, and control `running` with `onStop`; without `onStop`, the stop button is disabled during the reply.
Without `onAttach`, the button opens the system picker and creates chips with only name and size, without keeping the `File`; to actually send files, pass `onAttach` and control `attachments`.
By default, text and attachments are cleared after sending (`clearOnSubmit`); with empty `models` the menu disappears, and `model` with `onModelChange` makes the choice controlled.

quandoUsar: Show a model's reply arriving word by word, with natural pauses at commas, sentence ends and between paragraphs.
Real streams: if `text` grows with the new chunk appended at the end, the reveal continues from where it was instead of restarting.
Demos and onboarding where the person can pause, skip to the end or replay the reply from the status line.
quandoEvitar: Use `message` for replies that are already complete, with Markdown and copy, replay and rate actions; here the text is plain, split only into paragraphs.
Use `text-reveal` to reveal a short piece of interface with restrained motion, without a cursor or controls.
Use `loading-states` while no word has arrived yet.

teclado.acao: On the status line controls, pauses or resumes, skips to the end or replays; pause and skip are disabled when the text finishes.

acessibilidade: The animated words are `aria-hidden`; a hidden copy holds the whole text from the start, so the screen reader reads the complete reply, not one word at a time.
The status line is a `role="status"` with “Streaming”, “Paused” or “Complete” and, at the end, the total word count; the icon-only buttons have a fixed English `aria-label` and `title`.
With `controls={false}` there is no status line: nothing announces that the reply has finished, so notify in another way if that matters.
movimento: Each word rises from a soft blur behind a cursor; the pace slows at commas, sentence ends and between paragraphs.
The cursor breathes lightly while words arrive, blinks on pause and disappears at the end; a thin bar above the status line shows progress.
With “reduce motion” on, the whole text appears at once and the pause, skip and replay buttons disappear; the status line shows “Complete”.
responsivo: In a container stretched into a column, the status line stays at the bottom while the text grows above it, and wraps onto two lines when width runs short.
desempenho: Each word is a `<span>` and each step is a `setTimeout` followed by a re-render; for long replies that have already finished, pass `instant`.
notasIA: In a real stream, pass the accumulated text in `text`: appending at the end continues the reveal, but any other change restarts from zero; single line breaks become spaces.
`onComplete` fires once per run, as soon as all the words received so far have appeared; if the stream pauses between chunks, it fires before the real end, so use your own end signal.
When stopping a stream midway, keep only what the person saw with `takeWords(text, shown)`, using the number that came from `onProgress`; for history, use `instant`.

quandoUsar: Show an agent's plan as a list in which each step advances from pending to in progress and then to done.
Plans of known size, where it is worth showing “2 of 5” and a progress bar in the header.
Compact transcripts: collapsed, the list becomes a line that still shows the step in progress.
quandoEvitar: Use `agent-activity` when steps appear during the work, collect findings in chips or need a duration and an error state.
Use `stepper` to show which stage of a flow the person themselves is in.
Use `onboarding-checklist` when the person is the one who checks off tasks; here the steps are not clickable.

teclado.acao: On the header, collapses or opens the list; it is the component's only control.

acessibilidade: The header is a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; collapsed, it shows the step in progress, so the button's name keeps saying what is happening.
The count is an `aria-live="polite"` region that reads “N of M steps done”, and the bar is a `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow` equal to the done count and `aria-valuemax` equal to the total.
Each step starts with its state for screen readers only (“To do:”, “In progress:”, “Done:”); these texts, “All steps done” and the word “progress” in the bar's label are fixed in English.
movimento: The step in progress gets a spinner and a shimmer that runs across the label; on completion, the check mark lands with a small bounce and draws itself, and a strike crosses the label from left to right.
On mount the steps rise in sequence; steps added later open to their own height, the bar advances with a spring and the done count rolls.
With “reduce motion” on, everything only fades: the spinner stays still, there is no shimmer or check mark drawing, and the strike appears at once.
responsivo: Fills 100% of the parent; collapsed, the current step in the header truncates with an ellipsis on one line, and when open the step labels wrap.
notasIA: It is data-driven: pass `items` with a stable `id` and change each one's `status` (`pending`, `running`, `done`); there is no error state or duration.
`detail` only appears while the step is `running`: use it for the file or command of that moment.
It starts open; use `defaultOpen={false}` or the `open` and `onOpenChange` pair to collapse it, and `showProgress={false}` to remove the count and the bar.

quandoUsar: Ask permission inside the conversation before an agent runs a tool, showing its name and the exact arguments of the call.
When the person needs three outcomes: allow once, allow always or deny.
Long transcripts: after the decision, the request shrinks to a line that records the answer and can be reopened with “Change”.
quandoEvitar: Use `approval-card` for a business decision with a summary, details as label and value pairs and an “Undo”.
Use `tool-result` to record a call that has already run, with input, output and duration.
Use `dialog` when the decision must block the rest of the screen until it is made.

teclado.acao: Moves through “Deny”, “Always allow” and “Allow once”, in that order.
On a decision button, decides and moves focus to the “Change” of the result line, or to the request itself with `allowChange={false}`.
On “Change”, reopens the request and moves focus to “Allow once”.

acessibilidade: The root is a `role="group"` named “Permission request for” plus the `tool`, and the arguments sit in an “Arguments” group; a truncated value shows the full text in `title`.
When the decision comes from a button in the request, focus goes to the button that replaces it and does not fall to `body`; the result sits in a `role="status"` region.
“Wants to run”, “Permission request for” and “Arguments” are fixed in English; the button and result texts are translated through `labels`.
movimento: On decision, the request leaves upward with a light blur, the result line enters in its place and the frame follows the new height with a spring.
The result icon draws itself: a check mark for allow and a two-stroke X for deny.
With “reduce motion” on, swaps are opacity-only, the height changes instantly and the icons appear already drawn.
responsivo: It is a width container: below 21rem the two allow buttons share one row and “Deny” drops below them, at full width; in the result line, the argument disappears.
notasIA: Pause the agent until `onDecisionChange` returns `once`, `always` or `denied`; the “Always allow” rule is yours, because the component only records the choice.
`args` accepts an object (one `chave: valor` line per field, non-text values as JSON) or a string with line breaks; the result line shows only the first value.
Translate with `labels` (`once`, `always`, `deny`, `allowedOnce`, `allowedAlways`, `denied`, `change`); for history, render already-decided requests with `defaultDecision`.

quandoUsar: An agent's transcript: each tool call becomes a row with state, name, summary and duration, which opens to show input and output.
Calls still running: a timer counts live and the output shows waiting lines until the result arrives.
Debugging: objects appear as indented, colorized JSON, with a copy button on each block.
quandoEvitar: Use `tool-approval` before the call, when the person needs to allow or deny the execution.
Use `json-viewer` for large or nested JSON, with a collapsible tree, search and pagination.
Use `agent-activity` for a timeline of the agent's steps, without the input and output of each call.

teclado.acao: On the header, opens or collapses the record.
With the record open, moves through the copy buttons and the code blocks, which are focusable; collapsed, nothing in the body receives focus.
With focus on a code block, scroll content taller than 15rem (native scrolling).

acessibilidade: The header is a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; its name includes the state (“Running”, “Succeeded”, “Failed”), the tool, the summary and the duration with “running for” or “took”.
Collapsed, the body stays mounted but `inert`; each copy button has its own `aria-label` (“Copy input”, “Copy output”, “Copy error”).
While running, the output is a `role="status"` skeleton named “Waiting for the result”; all these texts are fixed in English.
movimento: The state swaps from a spinner to a badge that enters with a small bounce and a check mark or X that draws itself; on open, input and output rise in sequence.
The body opens and closes with a spring on the measured height and grows the same way when the result arrives with the record open.
With “reduce motion” on, the spinner and skeleton stop, the icons only fade, heights change instantly and the timer counts second by second.
responsivo: The tool name takes at most 55% of the row and the summary truncates with an ellipsis; in the code blocks long lines wrap, and above 15rem the block scrolls internally.
desempenho: Each record has a `ResizeObserver`; without `durationMs`, the `running` state also starts a 100 ms `setInterval` (1 s with “reduce motion”), which re-renders the record on each tick.
notasIA: When it finishes, change `status` to `success` or `error` and pass `durationMs` with `output` or `error`: without `durationMs`, the duration disappears when the state stops being `running`.
Objects passed as input and output become indented, colorized JSON; strings appear as they are, so send the object, not already-serialized text.
It starts collapsed; in a list, control `open` and `onOpenChange` to keep one record open at a time, as the demo does.

quandoUsar: The face of a voice assistant: shows whose turn it is, among idle, listening, thinking and speaking.
When there is a live audio level, from the microphone or playback, so the rings and bars follow the voice.
As the main button of the voice conversation, to start listening or interrupt speech, with `onPress`.
quandoEvitar: Use `loading-states` to indicate that the AI is thinking in a text conversation.
Use `button` with a microphone icon when you only need to turn recording on and off, without states or an audio level.
Use `loader` for generic loading, unrelated to voice.

teclado.acao: With `onPress`, the orb is a `<button>` and these keys activate it; without `onPress`, it does not receive focus.

acessibilidade: With `onPress` the orb is a `<button>` with `aria-label` equal to `label`; without `onPress`, it is a `role="img"` with the same name.

The state sits in a `role="status"`, visible as a caption or for screen readers only with `showLabel={false}`; the default texts (“Tap to talk”, “Listening”, “Thinking”, “Speaking”) change through `stateLabels`.
The `label` does not change with the state: if the tap does different things, such as start listening or interrupt, change the `label` for each state.
movimento: At rest the core breathes; listening, outlined rings open around it; thinking, an arc spins; speaking, the core fills with the accent color and the rings become soft discs.

While listening and speaking, the bars and rings follow `level` on every frame: the middle bar rises most and the outer rings follow with a looser spring, like a wave; while thinking, the bars undulate on their own.
With “reduce motion” on, each state becomes a still shape: fixed bars per state, rings at a single size, with no breathing, spinning or core pulse.
desempenho: Each of the five bars runs a per-frame callback while the orb is mounted, even at rest or with “reduce motion”; keep one orb per screen and unmount it outside the voice conversation.
Pass `level` as a `MotionValue`, for example fed by an `AnalyserNode`, to update every frame without rendering React; a number in `level` requires a render on every change.
notasIA: The orb does not read the microphone: compute the volume from 0 to 1 and pass it in `level`, preferably as a `MotionValue`; `state` decides colors, rings and the bars' movement.
Use `onPress` to start listening or interrupt speech, and change `label` according to what the tap does in each state.
`size` is the diameter in pixels, rings included (default 176); the orb does not shrink with the container, so choose the size with the smallest screen in mind.

quandoUsar: Demos or game areas with a play-money balance where the fun is cashing out before the curve crashes.
Show live motion: an exponential curve drawn every frame, the crash history in chips and the balance counting up to the new value.
Simulations and probability tests, with your own `random` to repeat rounds and `onRoundEnd` to record each result.
quandoEvitar: Do not use with real money or prizes: the balance is play money, the draw runs in the browser with `random` and nothing proves the round was fair.
Use `slide-game` when the result should come out at once, with no decision during the round.
Use `mines-game` when the person decides step by step, at their own pace, with no clock running.

teclado.acao: On the main button, bets, cashes out during the round and bets again; it is the same `<button>` for the whole round, so focus does not leave it.
In the bet field, confirms the value and clamps it between `minBet` and the balance.
Moves through reset balance, bet, ½, 2×, Max, auto cash-out and the main button; the fields are disabled during the round.

acessibilidade: The card is a `<section>` named by `title`, and a `role="status"` region announces the start, cash-out and crash of each round (“Round started…”, “Cashed out at…”, “Crashed at…”).
The chart is `aria-hidden`; the balance has a hidden “Play-money balance” text with the value, and the ½, 2× and Max shortcuts have their own `aria-label`.
When the action is not available, the main button uses `aria-disabled` instead of `disabled`, to stay focusable; all texts are in English.
movimento: The multiplier rises along an exponential curve redrawn every frame, with scales that stretch along with it, like a camera pulling back; the leading dot pulses.

On a crash, the curve and number switch to the danger color, a ring expands from the dot and the number shakes; a cash-out leaves a mark on the curve and the balance counts up to the new value with a “+” that rises.
With “reduce motion” on, the round continues, but the curve advances in a few steps per second, with no pulse, ring or shake.
responsivo: The card goes up to 34rem and is a container: the chart is 13rem to 16.5rem tall depending on width, and the bet and auto cash-out sit side by side from 26rem.
desempenho: During the round, a per-frame callback rewrites the SVG paths directly in the DOM, without rendering React; a `ResizeObserver` redraws the chart when it changes size.
notasIA: The balance is play money and can live in the component (`defaultBalance`) or outside it (`balance` with `onBalanceChange`); `onRoundEnd` reports the bet, crash point, cash-out and payout.
Pass a seeded `random` for tests or replays: it is called once per round, at bet time; `margin` (0 to 0.5) makes early crashes slightly more likely and `maxMultiplier` (50) caps the crash.
The folder brings its own copy of `play-money.tsx` (balance, bet field, button and history); `speed` controls the climb, with the multiplier equal to e^(`speed` × seconds).

quandoUsar: Demos or game areas with a play-money balance where each gem found raises the multiplier and the person decides when to stop.
Games playable by keyboard: the 5 × 5 board has roving focus and arrow keys to move between tiles.
Explain risk and reward: more mines give bigger jumps in the multiplier, which is the fair payout minus `margin`.
quandoEvitar: Do not use with real money or prizes: the balance is play money and the mines are drawn in the browser with `random`.
Use `crash-game` when the tension should come from time, cashing out before a live curve crashes.
Use `plinko-game` or `slide-game` when the result should come out on its own, with no decisions during the round.

teclado.acao: On the board, move focus between tiles and stop at the edge, without wrapping.
Move focus to the first or last tile of the current row.
On a closed tile during the round, flips the tile.
Enters the board at the last focused tile, the only one in the focus order, and then moves on to the bet and mine controls.
On the main button, bets, cashes out after the first gem and bets again; it is the same `<button>` the whole time.
In the bet field, confirms the value and clamps it between `minBet` and the balance.

acessibilidade: The board is a `role="group"` with roving focus (only one tile has `tabIndex={0}`), and each tile states row, column and state (“hidden”, “gem” or “mine”) in its `aria-label`.
Tiles already flipped or outside a round use `aria-disabled` and stay in the navigation; each move is announced in a `role="status"` region, and the mine count in another live region.
Balance, bet shortcuts and main button follow the pattern of the other games, with `aria-disabled` to keep focus; all texts are in English.
movimento: Tiles flip in 3D with a spring with a slight bounce; at the end of the round, the remaining ones flip in a wave starting from the focused tile, and a mine makes the board shake.
The multiplier makes a small hop on each gem, the mine count rolls in the direction of the adjustment and, on a new bet, the open tiles close in a diagonal sweep.
With “reduce motion” on, tiles flip instantly, with no wave, shake, staggered entrance or hover lift.
responsivo: The card goes up to 40rem and is a container: when narrow, the board sits above the controls; from 34rem they sit side by side, with the panel at 15rem and the board up to 24rem.
notasIA: `mines` (1 to 24) can be controlled with `onMinesChange`; at the end of each round, `onRoundEnd` brings gems, multiplier, outcome (`cashed-out` or `mine`), bet and payout.
`random` is only called at bet time, to hide the mines, so a seeded generator makes the board repeatable; finding all the gems ends the round with an automatic cash-out.
Like the other games, it is play money with its own copy of `play-money.tsx`; the balance can be controlled with `balance` and `onBalanceChange`.

quandoUsar: Demos or game areas with a play-money balance where several balls fall at the same time, each with its own bet.
Show a binomial distribution in action: the middle slots come up more often and pay less, the end ones are rare and pay more.
When the person chooses the risk (`low`, `medium`, `high`) and sees the multiplier table change instantly.
quandoEvitar: Do not use with real money or prizes: the balance is play money and each ball's path is drawn in the browser with `random`.
Use `crash-game` or `mines-game` when the person should decide during the round, cashing out before losing.
Use `slide-game` for one result per bet with the odds of each multiplier on display.

teclado.acao: On the “Drop a ball” button, drops a ball; repeating drops more, up to `maxBalls` falling together.
In the risk group, switches between “Low”, “Medium” and “High” (native radios); locked while balls are falling.
In the bet field, confirms the value and clamps it between `minBet` and the balance.
Moves through reset balance, bet, ½, 2×, Max, the selected risk and the drop button.

acessibilidade: The board is `aria-hidden`; the screen reader finds the list of slot multipliers, from left to right, and hears each landing (“Ball N landed on…”) in a `role="status"` region.
The risk is a group of native radios labeled “Risk”, each inside a `<label>`; the keyboard focus outline appears on the segment.
With several balls, each landing produces a new announcement; texts and announcements are fixed in English.
movimento: Each ball falls and, at each row, bounces left or right with a small upward impulse before gravity; the peg it touches lights up and grows.
The slot where the ball lands sinks and lights up, keeps a ring until the next drop, and the values swap with a slight slide when the risk changes.
With “reduce motion” on, no ball is drawn: the result comes out after a short pause and the slot only lights up, without sinking.
responsivo: The card goes up to 42rem and is a container: the board sits above the controls and moves to the side from 36rem, at most 27rem wide.
The board is an SVG that scales as a whole, and the slots follow its width; below 22rem the “×” disappears from the labels.
desempenho: A per-frame callback moves all the balls directly in the DOM, without rendering React on each step; `maxBalls` (8) limits how many fall together and `rows` ranges from 6 to 12.
notasIA: `risk` recomputes the table from each slot's binomial probability; for your own table, pass `multipliers` with exactly `rows + 1` values, otherwise it is ignored.
The bet leaves the balance when the ball is dropped and the payout comes in at landing, when `onDrop` arrives with slot, multiplier, bet and payout.
The bet field stays editable with balls falling and each ball keeps the bet from the moment it was dropped; it is play money, with its own copy of `play-money.tsx`.

quandoUsar: Demos or game areas with a play-money balance where a bet makes a strip of multipliers run and stop on its own.
When the odds should be on display: the list below the strip gives the percentage of each multiplier, computed from the weights.
Configurable draws: `tiles` defines the multipliers and the weight of each.
quandoEvitar: Do not use with real money or prizes: the balance is play money and the result is drawn in the browser with `random`.
Use `crash-game` or `mines-game` when the person should decide during the round.
Use `plinko-game` when several bets should run at the same time, with a risk the person chooses.

teclado.acao: On the main button, bets and releases the strip; during the slide it is `aria-disabled`, but keeps focus.
In the bet field, confirms the value and clamps it between `minBet` and the balance.

acessibilidade: The strip is `aria-hidden`; the result reaches the screen reader through the card's `role="status"` region (“Sliding with a bet of…”, “Landed on…”), and the odds sit in a labeled list.
Balance with hidden text, bet shortcuts with `aria-label` and main button with `aria-disabled` follow the pattern of the other games; all texts are in English.
movimento: The strip launches, spends most of the run slowing down and stops slightly off-center, settling on the tile with a spring; the marker's pointer ticks as tiles pass it.
On stopping, the winning tile grows with a shadow, the others fade and the marker grows along with it; on mount, the tiles enter from the center outward.
With “reduce motion” on, the strip does not run: it reappears at the final position with a short fade, with no pointer tick, no growth and no staggered entrance.
responsivo: The card goes up to 36rem and is a container: bet and button sit side by side from 28rem; the strip takes the full width and fades at the edges, with fixed 76 px tiles.
notasIA: `tiles` takes `multiplier` and `weight` (weight 2 comes up twice as often as weight 1); entries with zero weight or a negative multiplier are discarded, and with none valid the default table is restored.
`duration` (3.8 s) is the time of the run until it stops; `onRoundEnd` arrives when the strip stops, and `random` is only called at bet time, to draw the result and fill the strip.
The default table has weights that add up to 100 and pays 0.97 of the bet on average; it is play money, with its own copy of `play-money.tsx`.
